glance.label: Main Idea
glance.html: Moses sets up the tabernacle exactly as the LORD commanded, and then the cloud covers the tent and the glory of the LORD fills it. The book ends with God dwelling among His redeemed people and leading them by cloud and fire.

glance.label: Setting
glance.html: At Mount Sinai, nearly a year after the exodus, the tabernacle is raised on the first day of the second year. The chapter closes the building account and the book.

glance.label: Chapter Outline
glance.html:
• Exodus 40:1–8 — The LORD Commands Moses to Set Up the Tabernacle

  • Exodus 40:9–15 — The LORD Commands the Anointing of the Tabernacle and the Priests

  • Exodus 40:16–33 — Moses Raises the Tabernacle as the LORD Commanded

  • Exodus 40:34–35 — The Glory of the LORD Fills the Tabernacle

  • Exodus 40:36–38 — The Cloud and Fire Lead Israel Throughout Their Journeys

glance.label: Key Verse
glance.html: “Then the cloud covered the tabernacle of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” (Exodus 40:34)

cards.title: The Heart of the Chapter
cards.html:
The LORD tells Moses to raise the tabernacle on the first day of the new year, in the month He had set apart at Passover. Moses is to place each furnishing, anoint everything, and wash, clothe, and anoint Aaron and his sons. Then Moses obeys: “according to all that the LORD had commanded him, so he did” (40:16). Piece by piece the dwelling goes up, and seven times the text repeats that each part was done “as the LORD had commanded Moses” (40:19). Finally, “So Moses finished the work” (40:33).

Then God acts. “Then the cloud covered the tabernacle of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle” (40:34). The glory that rested on Sinai now comes to live in the middle of the camp. The presence is so full and holy that even Moses cannot enter. From that day on, the cloud over the tabernacle sets Israel’s course. When it lifts, they travel; when it stays, they wait. The book that began with Israel crying out in slavery ends with God dwelling among His people, just as He promised: “I will dwell among the children of Israel and will be their God” (29:45).

cards.title: Chapter Sections
cards.html:
Exodus 40:1–8 — The LORD Commands Moses to Set Up the Tabernacle

The LORD tells Moses to set up the tabernacle on the first day of the first month. He gives the order for placing the ark behind the veil, the furnishings of the holy place, the altar and laver outside, and the court all around.

Exodus 40:9–15 — The LORD Commands the Anointing of the Tabernacle and the Priests

Moses is to anoint the tabernacle and everything in it, making it holy. He is also to wash, clothe, and anoint Aaron and his sons, for their anointing will be a lasting priesthood through their generations.

Exodus 40:16–33 — Moses Raises the Tabernacle as the LORD Commanded

Moses does everything the LORD commanded. He raises the tabernacle, puts the Testimony in the ark, sets each furnishing in its place, begins the service of bread, lamp, incense, and sacrifice, and finishes the work.

Exodus 40:34–35 — The Glory of the LORD Fills the Tabernacle

The cloud covers the tent of meeting and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle. Moses cannot enter because the cloud rests on it and the glory fills it.

Exodus 40:36–38 — The Cloud and Fire Lead Israel Throughout Their Journeys

From then on, Israel travels when the cloud lifts from the tabernacle and stays when it remains. The cloud by day and fire by night stay over the tabernacle in the sight of all Israel throughout their journeys.

cards.title: Why This Chapter Matters
cards.html:
Exodus 40 shows the goal of redemption. God did not only bring Israel out of Egypt; He brought them to Himself so that He could live among them. Their obedience prepared the place, but the filling was God’s own gift. His presence is both near and holy, so near that it fills the tabernacle in the midst of the camp and so holy that even Moses must stand outside.

That story continues in Jesus, the Word who “dwelt among us” and whose glory His disciples saw (John 1:14). Through Him we draw near to God, and Scripture ends with the promise that “the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them” (Revelation 21:3). Like Israel, God’s people today follow where His presence leads.

cards.title: Key Themes to Watch For
cards.html:
Obedience to God’s word. Moses does everything “as the LORD had commanded” (40:19, 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 32).

God’s glory fills His dwelling. The cloud covers the tent and His glory fills the tabernacle (40:34).

Nearness and holiness together. God lives among His people, yet even Moses cannot enter the glory-filled tent (40:35).

God leads His people. Israel travels and waits at the direction of the cloud and fire (40:36–38).

The purpose of the exodus fulfilled. God dwells among the people He redeemed, as He promised (29:45–46; 40:34–38).

cards.title: Key Words & Concepts
cards.html:
Tabernacle of the tent of meeting (40:2). God’s portable dwelling, the place where He would meet with His people.

Anoint (40:9). To apply holy oil, setting a person or object apart for God’s service.

Everlasting priesthood (40:15). The lasting priestly office God gave to Aaron and his descendants.

Cloud (40:34). The visible sign of the LORD’s presence that covered the tabernacle and guided Israel.

Glory of the LORD (40:34). The weighty, visible splendor of God’s presence filling His dwelling.

focus: Exodus 40 brings the book to its goal: the LORD commands Moses to set up and anoint the tabernacle, Moses does everything as the LORD commanded, and then the cloud covers the tent and “the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle” (Exodus 40:34). The book closes with the LORD dwelling among His people and leading them by cloud and fire throughout all their journeys.

sections.title: The LORD Commands Moses to Set Up the Tabernacle
sections.summary: The LORD tells Moses to set up the tabernacle on the first day of the first month. He is to place the ark behind the veil, the table, lampstand, and incense altar in the tent, the altar of burnt offering and the laver outside, and the court all around.

sections.title: The LORD Commands the Anointing of the Tabernacle and the Priests
sections.summary: Moses is to anoint the tabernacle, its furnishings, the altar, and the laver so that they are holy. He is to wash, clothe, and anoint Aaron and his sons, “for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations” (Exodus 40:15).

sections.title: Moses Raises the Tabernacle as the LORD Commanded
sections.summary: “Thus Moses did; according to all that the LORD had commanded him, so he did” (Exodus 40:16): on the first day of the first month of the second year he raises the tabernacle and places the Testimony in the ark, the ark behind the veil, and the table, lampstand, and gold altar in the tent. He sets the altar of burnt offering and the laver before the door, raises the court, and “So Moses finished the work” (Exodus 40:33).

sections.title: The Glory of the LORD Fills the Tabernacle
sections.summary: “Then the cloud covered the tabernacle of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle” (Exodus 40:34). Moses is not able to enter the tent because the cloud rests on it and the glory fills it.

sections.title: The Cloud and Fire Lead Israel Throughout Their Journeys
sections.summary: Whenever the cloud is taken up from the tabernacle, Israel sets out, and when it remains, they stay. The cloud of the LORD is over the tabernacle by day and fire by night, in the sight of all Israel, “throughout all their journeys” (Exodus 40:38).

1.brief: The LORD speaks to Moses. The final instructions of the book concern raising God’s dwelling.
1.explain:
“Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:”

The final instructions of the book concern raising God’s dwelling.

2.brief: “On the first day of the first month you shall set up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.” The dwelling is to be raised at the start of a new year, nearly a year after the exodus.
2.explain:
“On the first day of the first month you shall set up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.”

The tabernacle is to be set up “on the first day of the first month.” This was almost a year after the exodus (12:2; 19:1). The dwelling is raised at the start of a new year.

3.brief: Moses is to put the ark of the Testimony in it and screen it off with the veil. The holiest furnishing is placed first.
3.explain:
“You shall put in it the ark of the Testimony, and partition off the ark with the veil.”

The ark is placed first and screened off “with the veil.” The holiest furnishing comes first.

4.brief: Moses is to bring in the table and set its things in order, and bring in the lampstand and light its lamps. The holy place is arranged for service.
4.explain:
“You shall bring in the table and arrange the things that are to be set in order on it;”

The table is brought in and its bread arranged.

“and you shall bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.”

The lampstand is lit. The holy place is arranged for service.

5.brief: Moses is to set the gold altar of incense before the ark of the Testimony and put up the screen at the door of the tabernacle. The LORD directs both the altar’s place and the entrance screen.
5.explain:
“You shall also set the altar of gold for the incense before the ark of the Testimony,”

The incense altar stands “before the ark,” in front of the veil.

“and put up the screen for the door of the tabernacle.”

The “screen” is hung at the entrance of the tent.

6.brief: Moses is to set the altar of burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle. The place of sacrifice stands at the entrance.
6.explain:
“Then you shall set the altar of the burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.”

The altar of sacrifice stands at the entrance.

7.brief: Moses is to set the laver between the tent and the altar and put water in it. The place of washing stands on the way into God’s presence.
7.explain:
“And you shall set the laver between the tabernacle of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.”

The “laver” stands between the altar and the tent. The place of washing stands on the way into God’s presence.

8.brief: Moses is to set up the court all around and hang the screen at its gate. The whole sanctuary is enclosed.
8.explain:
“You shall set up the court all around, and hang up the screen at the court gate.”

The court encloses the whole sanctuary.

9.brief: Moses is to take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it, so that it will be holy. The dwelling is to be set apart for God.
9.explain:
“And you shall take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle and all that is in it;”

The “anointing oil” is applied to the tent and all its contents (30:26–29).

“and you shall hallow it and all its utensils, and it shall be holy.”

The dwelling is set apart for God.

10.brief: Moses is to anoint the altar of burnt offering and its utensils, and “The altar shall be most holy.” The place of sacrifice is consecrated.
10.explain:
“You shall anoint the altar of the burnt offering and all its utensils, and consecrate the altar.”

The altar is anointed.

“The altar shall be most holy.”

The place of sacrifice is consecrated as “most holy.”

11.brief: Moses is to anoint the laver and its base and consecrate it. Every furnishing is to be set apart.
11.explain:
“And you shall anoint the laver and its base, and consecrate it.”

Every furnishing is set apart.

12.brief: Moses is to bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle and wash them with water. The priests are to be cleansed.
12.explain:
“Then you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle of meeting and wash them with water.”

The priests are washed at the entrance (29:4).

13.brief: Moses is to put the holy garments on Aaron, anoint him, and consecrate him to minister as priest. Aaron is to be set apart for his office.
13.explain:
“You shall put the holy garments on Aaron, and anoint him and consecrate him, that he may minister to Me as priest.”

Aaron is clothed, anointed, and consecrated (29:5–7). Leviticus 8 records this ceremony.

14.brief: Moses is to bring Aaron’s sons and clothe them with tunics. The other priests are to be clothed.
14.explain:
“And you shall bring his sons and clothe them with tunics.”

Aaron’s sons are clothed (29:8).

15.brief: Moses is to anoint them as he anointed their father, “for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.” God establishes the priesthood permanently.
15.explain:
“You shall anoint them, as you anointed their father, that they may minister to Me as priests;”

The sons are anointed too.

“for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.”

Their anointing establishes “an everlasting priesthood.” Hebrews 7:11–28 explains that Christ has come as a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek, with a better priesthood.

16.brief: “Thus Moses did; according to all that the LORD had commanded him, so he did.” Moses obeys God’s instructions completely.
16.explain:
“Thus Moses did; according to all that the LORD had commanded him, so he did.”

Moses obeys completely. The rest of the section shows him doing exactly what God said.

17.brief: In the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle is raised up. The dwelling is set up on the very day God appointed.
17.explain:
“And it came to pass in the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was raised up.”

The tabernacle is “raised up” on the very day God appointed (40:2).

18.brief: Moses raises the tabernacle, fastens its sockets, sets up its boards, puts in its bars, and raises its pillars. The frame is assembled.
18.explain:
“So Moses raised up the tabernacle, fastened its sockets, set up its boards, put in its bars, and raised up its pillars.”

Moses assembles the frame, from the silver sockets up.

19.brief: Moses spreads the tent over the tabernacle and puts the covering on top, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” The coverings are put in place as God directed.
19.explain:
“And he spread out the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering of the tent on top of it,”

The coverings are spread over the frame.

“as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

The refrain of obedience runs through the section seven times (40:19, 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 32).

20.brief: Moses puts the Testimony into the ark, inserts the poles, and puts the mercy seat on top. God’s covenant now rests beneath the mercy seat.
20.explain:
“He took the Testimony and put it into the ark,”

The tablets of the law go into the ark (25:16).

“inserted the poles through the rings of the ark, and put the mercy seat on top of the ark.”

The “mercy seat” covers the ark. God’s covenant now rests beneath the place of meeting.

21.brief: Moses brings the ark into the tabernacle, hangs the veil, and screens off the ark, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” The Most Holy is set in order.
21.explain:
“And he brought the ark into the tabernacle, hung up the veil of the covering, and partitioned off the ark of the Testimony, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

The ark is brought in and the veil hung. The Most Holy Place is set in order.

22.brief: Moses puts the table in the tabernacle on the north side, outside the veil. The holy place is furnished.
22.explain:
“He put the table in the tabernacle of meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil;”

The table goes on the north side of the holy place (26:35).

23.brief: Moses sets the bread in order on it before the LORD, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” The showbread is placed before God.
23.explain:
“and he set the bread in order upon it before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

The showbread is placed “before the LORD.”

24.brief: Moses puts the lampstand across from the table on the south side. The light of the holy place is placed.
24.explain:
“He put the lampstand in the tabernacle of meeting, across from the table, on the south side of the tabernacle;”

The lampstand goes on the south side.

25.brief: Moses lights the lamps before the LORD, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” Light now shines in God’s dwelling.
25.explain:
“and he lit the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

Moses “lit the lamps.” Light now shines in God’s dwelling.

26.brief: Moses puts the gold altar in the tabernacle in front of the veil. The altar of incense stands before the Most Holy.
26.explain:
“He put the gold altar in the tabernacle of meeting in front of the veil;”

The incense altar stands before the Most Holy Place.

27.brief: Moses burns sweet incense on it, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” Worship begins in the holy place.
27.explain:
“and he burned sweet incense on it, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

Moses “burned sweet incense.” Worship begins in the holy place. Until Aaron is consecrated, Moses performs these first priestly acts.

28.brief: Moses hangs the screen at the door of the tabernacle. The entrance to the tent is closed.
28.explain:
“He hung up the screen at the door of the tabernacle.”

The entrance screen is hung.

29.brief: Moses sets the altar of burnt offering before the door and offers the burnt offering and grain offering on it, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” Sacrifice begins at God’s dwelling.
29.explain:
“And he put the altar of burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting,”

The altar is placed at the entrance.

“and offered upon it the burnt offering and the grain offering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

Moses makes the first offerings. Sacrifice begins at God’s dwelling.

30.brief: Moses sets the laver between the tent and the altar and puts water in it for washing. The place of cleansing is ready.
30.explain:
“He set the laver between the tabernacle of meeting and the altar, and put water there for washing;”

The laver is filled with water. The place of cleansing is ready.

31.brief: Moses, Aaron, and his sons wash their hands and feet from the laver. Those who serve are cleansed.
31.explain:
“and Moses, Aaron, and his sons would wash their hands and their feet with water from it.”

Those who serve wash their “hands” and “feet” (30:19).

32.brief: Whenever they enter the tabernacle or come near the altar, they wash, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” Cleansing becomes a regular part of their service.
32.explain:
“Whenever they went into the tabernacle of meeting, and when they came near the altar, they washed, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

Cleansing becomes a regular part of their service.

33.brief: Moses raises the court around the tabernacle and altar and hangs the screen at the gate, “So Moses finished the work.” The whole dwelling is complete as God commanded.
33.explain:
“And he raised up the court all around the tabernacle and the altar, and hung up the screen of the court gate.”

The court is set up around everything.

“So Moses finished the work.”

The words echo Genesis 2:2, where God finished His work. The whole dwelling is complete as God commanded. Human obedience has done its part. Now God acts.

34.brief: “Then the cloud covered the tabernacle of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” The goal of the book is reached as God’s glory fills the dwelling His people prepared.
34.explain:
“Then the cloud covered the tabernacle of meeting,”

The “cloud” that led Israel from Egypt (13:21) now “covered the tabernacle.”

“and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.”

This is the goal of the book. God brought Israel out of Egypt to dwell among them (29:45–46). Now He does. The filling is God’s act, not the people’s achievement. The God whose presence was threatened after the calf (33:3) now dwells in the midst of His forgiven people. In Christ, God’s glory came to dwell with His people in human flesh: “the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory” (John 1:14).
34.notes: The same thing happened when Solomon’s temple was dedicated (1 Kings 8:10–11).

35.brief: Moses cannot enter the tabernacle because the cloud rests on it and the glory of the LORD fills it. God’s presence is so full and holy that even Moses must stand outside.
35.explain:
“And Moses was not able to enter the tabernacle of meeting,”

Even “Moses was not able to enter.” The man who spoke with God face to face must stand outside.

“because the cloud rested above it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.”

God’s presence is so full and holy that no one can come in. The nearness of God and the weight of His holiness stand together. Under the new covenant, believers have boldness to enter the Holiest by the blood of Jesus, through the new and living way He opened (Hebrews 10:19–22).
35.notes: Leviticus 1:1 continues directly from this verse: the LORD calls to Moses from the tabernacle of meeting and gives instructions for sacrifice, the way God provides for sinful people to draw near.

36.brief: Whenever the cloud is taken up from the tabernacle, Israel goes onward in all their journeys. God’s presence now leads His people.
36.explain:
“Whenever the cloud was taken up from above the tabernacle,”

When the cloud lifted from the tent, Israel knew it was time to move.

“the children of Israel would go onward in all their journeys.”

God’s presence now leads His people from the center of their camp.

37.brief: If the cloud is not taken up, Israel does not journey until it lifts. Israel’s movement depends entirely on God’s direction.
37.explain:
“But if the cloud was not taken up, then they did not journey till the day that it was taken up.”

If the cloud stayed, they stayed. Israel’s movement depended entirely on God’s direction. They waited when the cloud rested and set out when it lifted. Numbers 9:15–23 describes this pattern in detail.

38.brief: “For the cloud of the LORD was above the tabernacle by day, and fire was over it by night,” in the sight of all Israel “throughout all their journeys.” The book ends with God dwelling among His redeemed people and leading them, a hope fulfilled in Christ, who dwelt among us.
38.explain:
“For the cloud of the LORD was above the tabernacle by day, and fire was over it by night,”

The cloud by day and fire by night stayed “above the tabernacle.”

“in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.”

Every Israelite could see it on every stage of the way. The book that began with Israel enslaved in Egypt ends with God dwelling among His redeemed people and leading them. That hope is fulfilled in Christ, who dwelt among us, and Revelation 21:3 looks to the final day: “Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them, and they shall be His people.”
